summary: Richard P. Boyle earned degrees at CU Boulder, McGill, and Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa (Ph.D. 1982), with postdoctorates at Düsseldorf and Washington University, and studied under Joshu Sasaki. He taught at UCLA, OHSU (1986–2000), and UNM (attested 2015).

Richard P. Hayes is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal, later holding posts at Toronto, McGill (1988–2003), UNM (2003–2013), and Leiden University.

A scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Richard Payne studied under Frits Staal. He served as dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1996, 2007) and held posts at the University of Chicago and Numata Center.
Richard Peter Hottelet was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Narayan Hemandas Samtani and was affiliated with the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1971.

Richard Phené Spiers (1838–1916) was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at King's College London from circa 1855 to 1858 and at the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts from circa 1858 to 1861.

Richard Pischel (1849–1908) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate and habilitation at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler. He held professorships at Kiel (1875), the University of Halle (1885–1902), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1908).

Richard Polenberg (1937–2020) was a historian of American history who studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University. He was a professor at Cornell University from 1966 to 2011 and a Fulbright Visiting Professor at Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1978–1979).

Richard S. Cohen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Walter M. Spink and Luis Oscar Gómez. He held posts at Rhodes College, the University of Pennsylvania, and UC San Diego as Associate Professor.

Richard Schechner studied at Cornell University, the University of Iowa, and Tulane University. Beginning around 1967, he held a post as University Professor at New York University's Tisch School of the Arts.

Richard Scherzl studied at Charles University, Saint Petersburg State University, and the University of Kharkiv. He directed Odesa University in 1886 and served at the University of Kharkiv as Docent (1882), extraordinary professor (1890), and ordinary professor (1894).

Indologist Richard Schmidt studied at Halle under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He served as a lecturer at Halle, librarian for the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1904–1910), and ordinary professor at the University of Münster from 1910.

Richard Shilleto (1809–1876) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He completed his education at Repton School, Shrewsbury School, and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1828–1832), and taught Robert Alexander Neil.

Indologist Richard Simon (1865–1934) studied at Leipzig, Freiburg, Berlin, and Halle, earning his PhD under Richard Pischel. He later served as Privatdozent (1892) and extraordinary professor (1906) at the University of Munich.

Richard Sorabji is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Pembroke College, Oxford. He served on the faculty at Cornell University (~1962–1970), King's College London (~1970–2000), and Gresham College (~2000–2006).

Linguist Richard Sproat studied at UC San Diego (BA) and MIT (PhD 1985). He held positions at Bell Labs, AT&T Labs, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Oregon Health & Science University, Google, and Sakana AI.

Richard Stothert (1833–1898) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Glasgow and earned an M.A. from the University of Edinburgh. He served as Principal of Wilson College, Mumbai, from 1876 to 1884.

Richard Sylvan (1935–1996) was a philosopher who studied at Victoria University of Wellington and Princeton University. He held academic posts at the University of Sydney (~1962–1964) and the Australian National University, where he became a fellow in 1971.

Richard Taupier, working in history, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian, and Buddhist studies, earned a master's and doctorate at UMass Amherst. He served as UMass Amherst's Associate Director of Research Development and as a Visiting Lecturer at Smith College.

Indologist Richard W. Lariviere earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher. He served as Dean at UT Austin, Provost at the University of Kansas, and President of both the University of Oregon and the Field Museum.

Richard Wilhelm (1873–1930) was a sinologist who studied at the University of Tübingen (~1891–1895). He served as a visiting professor at Peking University (1923) and held the chair of Sinology at Goethe University Frankfurt from 1924, founding it in 1925.
